correctness.rationale: Orthogonality of B^k (because B(0)=0) gives psi_B in H2 and its imaginary boundary part exactly ±pi/2. The bounded coanalytic-representative symbol bar(psi_B)-psi_B=-2i Im psi_B has L-infinity norm pi, proving Hankel boundedness and upper norm. Compressing H on inputs B^(2k) and outputs bar(B)^(2j+1) yields exact generalized Hilbert matrix A_jk=1/(j+k+1/2) with norm at least pi via x_j=1/sqrt(j) on logarithmic blocks; the integral comparison gives pi as log L coefficient, and shifting supports to L..L^2 gives weakly null unit vectors so even the essential norm >=pi. Uniform Poisson identity for kernel energy plus the analytic identity P[(psi_B-psi_B(a))^2]=0 makes real and imaginary centered variances equal; with (Im psi_B)^2=pi^2/4 on boundary this gives the exact formula and maximizing set where Im psi_B(a)=0, equivalent to B(a) real in (-1,1). I independently checked H2 coefficient sum to pi^2/2 within <1e-5 and finite generalized Hilbert Rayleigh lower bounds; these numerical checks are not proofs of pi essential norm.
